x: Our lads soon began to show their paces and there was little doubt throughout the race as to the ultimate result. Thompson of Met. W.C. only 21 years of age, set up a terrific pace and by the time Crawley was reached had open up a gap of over 8 minutes.
After the 10 laps we moved out on to the road with George leading from Bryan Hawkins and myself, Bob Goodall, McFarlane, and Don Thompson with the French team.

A strong Metropolitan W.C. led by Thompson, won the team title with 19 points, but we were a worthy second with 33. George Checkley confirmed his previous week's success finishing 5th with Hugh 6th, Bob 10th and Harry 12th.
But as was the case with the Polytechnic Marathon on the same day, the rain appears to have given the competitors extra speed with the result that the winner, Brian Thompson of the Met.
Meanwhile nearer the front Don Thompson was making it quite obvious that he was out to break the course record and was minutes ahead of schedule.
Thompson (Met.W.C.) and three Belgrave lads - G.
Early in the race George Checkley and Thompson of Met. W.C., when leading, unfortunately went off course to the extent of about six minutes.
At half-distance Misson(Met.W.C.) had taken the lead with Johnson(Sheffield) near at hand followed by Don Thompson(Met) and Eric, taking things reasonably easy, fourth.
Approaching the end of the first lap Miller, Thompson, Glover, Bedford and Shippen were in close attendance around tenth position with John Moore moving through fast after his mishap.
Mike Maynard set a fast pace at the start and was comfortably leading after a mile from John Moore and Chris Thompson with Clive Shippen and the Blackheath captain, A.W.

The Brighton this year again dissolved into two distinct races, the two Metropolitan men, Thompson and Misson were locked together until just after Crawley, but Belgrave supporters were more interested in the third place and team race.

Though, Thompson striding to a great win in the 50 Kilos walk; Radford flashing to a bronze medal in the 100 metres; Elliott toying with the world's best over 1500 metres; "wild-man" Cerutty running on to the track; Avril Williams throwing the javelin beyond the Olympic record and into second place,…

…imbs up the horse-rides in the darkness of Tuesday evenings chasing the unseen figures of Robinson, Miller, Shippen and Thompson; out on the dimly lit roads of Wimbledon on Thursdays, gasping behind Linstead, Dabbs, Gebbett & Co. as they did the "seven hills"; sometimes on the "Warren 9" with Bird,…
To go to the head of the field and win the race and to be acclaimed with the names of Whitlock, Baker, Thompson, Pamich, Middleton is something extra.
